textbookVisuals.visualPurpose: The Phase I → Phase II → Excretion flow diagram
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: The Drug Metabolism flow diagram: two input rails (Lipophilic drugs at top-left; Polar drugs (water-soluble) at top-right) feeding into Phase I (predominantly CYP450-dependent) and Phase II boxes; Phase I contains the four reaction types (Reduction, Oxidation, Hydrolysis, Methylation) and outputs Slightly polar metabolite (active or inactive) plus Reactive oxygen metabolites; Phase II contains the three conjugation reactions (Glucuronidation, Acetylation, Sulfation) and outputs Very polar, hydrophilic metabolite (except acetylated metabolite); the final Excretion box shows Serum (urine, sweat) and bile (stool) routes. The Phase I output flows into Phase II (sequential) but the page notes the reactions 'do not have to take place sequentially' (eg, phase I can follow phase II, or take place as a single reaction). A vector figure (no raster).

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.visualPurpose: The zero-order elimination graph
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: The zero-order elimination plot: y-axis 'Drug plasma concentration' (with ↑), x-axis 'Time (h)'. Cp falls in a straight LINE — the elimination rate (=slope) is constant at 2 U/h regardless of Cp (the graph labels 2 U/h twice along the line). Horizontal dashed guides mark the successive halvings (4 → 2 → 1 → 0.5) and the three half-life intervals are bracketed beneath the x-axis: 'First t1/2 >', 'Second t1/2 >', 'Third t1/2' — each successive interval is SHORTER. The graph's rule annotation reads 'Time of t1/2 ↑ as concentration ↑' (half-life is NOT constant in zero-order elimination; it lengthens as concentration rises). A vector figure (no raster).
textbookVisuals.kypLocation: the registry visual (the zero-order panel of the EliminationOfDrugsMap)

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.visualPurpose: The first-order elimination graph
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: The first-order elimination plot: y-axis 'Drug plasma concentration' (with ↑), x-axis 'Time (h)'. Cp falls on an exponential CURVE — the elimination rate (=slope) is labeled at four successive positions (4 U/h, 2 U/h, 1 U/h, 0.5 U/h) and FALLS in proportion to the concentration. The three half-life intervals are bracketed beneath the x-axis: 'First t1/2 =', 'Second t1/2 =', 'Third t1/2' — every interval is EQUAL. The graph's rule annotation reads 'Time of t1/2 is constant as concentration ↑' (half-life is constant in first-order elimination). A vector figure (no raster).
textbookVisuals.kypLocation: the registry visual (the first-order panel of the EliminationOfDrugsMap)

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.visualPurpose: The zero-order vs first-order comparison rows
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: The two comparison rows printed under the 'Elimination of drugs' header. Zero-order row: 'Rate of elimination is constant regardless of Cp (ie, constant amount of drug eliminated per unit time). Cp ↓ linearly with time. Examples of drugs—Phenytoin, Ethanol, and Aspirin (at high or toxic concentrations → ↑ salicylate saturation → zero-order elimination).' with the side note 'Capacity-limited elimination.' First-order row: 'Rate of first-order elimination is directly proportional to the drug concentration (ie, constant fraction of drug eliminated per unit time). Cp ↓ exponentially with time. Applies to most drugs.' with the side note 'Flow-dependent elimination.' Pure text, no figures.

Below the x-axis the graph annotates the pKa axis: 'pKa = more acidic' (left) and 'pKa = more basic' (right). A vector figure (no raster).

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.visualPurpose: The AUTONOMIC/SOMATIC overview schematic (the section's single figure — the classic autonomic nervous system receptor map)
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: The section's entire figure: a left-to-right schematic of the AUTONOMIC division (subdivided Parasympathetic and Sympathetic) and the SOMATIC division. The CNS column at the left (Brainstem above, Spinal cord below) gives off three pathways. PARASYMPATHETIC: 'Preganglionic neuron (long)' → ganglion near the organ (ACh on Nn) → 'Postganglionic neuron (short)' → ACh on 'M₁, M₂, M₃' → 'Smooth muscle, gland cells, nerve terminals, cardiac muscle'. SYMPATHETIC: 'Preganglionic neuron (short)' → the 'Sympathetic chain' (ACh on Nn) → 'Postganglionic neuron (long)' → NE on 'α1, α2, β1, β2' → 'Smooth muscle, gland cells, nerve terminals, cardiac muscle'; a cholinergic sympathetic fiber → ACh on 'M₃' → 'Sweat glands'; a dopaminergic branch → D on 'D1' → 'Renal vasculature smooth muscle'; and the 'Adrenal gland (medulla)' limb — directly innervated by the preganglionic fiber (ACh on Nn), secreting Epi + NE into the 'Blood (catecholamine transmission)' onto 'α1, α2, β1, β2' at 'Cardiac muscle, vessels'. Zone 1 (APPLICATION/ACTIONS/NOTES-EXAMPLES, ten rows): 'Angina pectoris' → '↓ heart rate and contractility → ↓ O2 consumption'; 'Glaucoma' → '↓ production of aqueous humor' | 'Timolol'; 'Heart failure' → 'Blockade of neurohormonal stress → prevention of deleterious cardiac remodeling → ↓ mortality' | 'Bisoprolol, carvedilol, metoprolol (β-blockers curb mortality)'; 'Hypertension' → '↓ cardiac output, ↓ renin secretion (due to β1receptor blockade on JG cells)'; 'Hyperthyroidism/thyroid storm' → 'Symptom control (↓ heart rate, ↓ tremor)' | 'Propranolol'; 'Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy' → '↓ heart rate → ↑ filling time, relieving obstruction'; 'Migraine' → '↓ nitric oxide production' | 'Effective for prevention'; 'Myocardial infarction' → '↓ O2 demand (short-term), ↓ mortality (long-term)'; 'Supraventricular tachycardia (eg, atrial fibrillation)' → '↓ AV conduction velocity (class II antiarrhythmic)' | 'Metoprolol, esmolol'; 'Variceal bleeding' → '↓ hepatic venous pressure gradient and portal hypertension (prophylactic use)' | 'Nadolol, propranolol, carvedilol for no portal circulation'. Zone 2 (ADVERSE EFFECTS): 'Erectile dysfunction, cardiovascular (bradycardia, AV block, HF), CNS (seizures, sleep alterations), dyslipidemia (metoprolol), masked hypoglycemia, asthma/COPD exacerbations' + 'Use of β-blockers for acute cocaine-associated chest pain remains controversial due to unsubstantiated concern for unopposed α-adrenergic stimulation'. Zone 3 (SELECTIVITY, four rows with printed mnemonics): 'β1-selective antagonists (β1 > β2)—atenolol, betaxolol, bisoprolol, esmolol, metoprolol' | 'Selective antagonists mostly go from A to M (β1 with 1st half of alphabet)'; 'Nonselective antagonists (β1 = β2)—nadolol, propranolol, timolol' | 'NonZelective antagonists mostly go from N to Z (β2 with 2nd half of alphabet)'; 'Nonselective β-adrenergic, α1-selective antagonists—carvedilol, labetalol' | 'Nonselective β-adrenergic and α1-selective antagonists have modified suffixes (instead of “-olol”)'; 'Nebivolol combines cardiac-selective β1-adrenergic blockade with stimulation of β3 -receptors (activate NO synthase in the vasculature and ↓ SVR)' | 'NebivOlol increases NO'. Carried VERBATIM as the note's two table blocks and conveyed as ONE original KYP selectivity/application map (the mechanism strip, the four fork cards, the ten-use grid, the caution strip, the boundary strip, the reading-rule footer) — no artwork reproduced.

textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: ONE FOUR-COLUMN TEXT TABLE + TWO FOOTNOTES (PURE TEXT — ZERO rasters on pdf 267; pdfimages returns no rows; COPYRIGHTED, never reproduced as artwork). Header: 'Phosphodiesterase inhibitors' + the intro sentence 'Phosphodiesterase (PDE) inhibitors inhibit PDE, which catalyzes the hydrolysis of cAMP and/or cGMP, and thereby increase cAMP and/or cGMP. These inhibitors have varying specificity for PDE isoforms and thus have different clinical uses.' Rows (TYPE / MECHANISM / USES / ADVERSE): 'Nonspecific PDE inhibitor / Theophylline': '↓ cAMP hydrolysis → ↑ cAMP → bronchial smooth muscle relaxation → bronchodilation' | 'COPD/asthma (rarely used)' | 'Cardiotoxicity (eg, tachycardia, arrhythmia), neurotoxicity (eg, seizures, headache), abdominal pain'. 'PDE-5 inhibitors / Sildenafil, vardenafil, tadalafil, avanafil': '↓ hydrolysis of cGMP → ↑ cGMP → ↑ smooth muscle relaxation by enhancing NO activity → pulmonary vasodilation and ↑ blood flow in corpus cavernosum fills the penis' | 'Erectile dysfunction / Pulmonary hypertension / Benign prostatic hyperplasia (tadalafil only)' | 'Facial flushing, headache, dyspepsia, hypotension in patients taking nitrates; "hot and sweaty," then headache, heartburn, hypotension' + 'Sildenafil only: cyanopia (blue-tinted vision) via inhibition of PDE-6 (six) in retina'. 'PDE-4 inhibitor / Roflumilast': '↑ cAMP in neutrophils, granulocytes, and bronchial epithelium' | 'Severe COPD' | 'Abdominal pain, weight loss, depression, anxiety, insomnia'. 'PDE-3 inhibitor / Milrinone': 'In cardiomyocytes: ↑ cAMP → ↑ Ca2+ influx → ↑ ionotropy and chronotropy / In vascular smooth muscle: ↑ cAMP → MLCK inhibition → vasodilation → ↓ preload and afterload' | 'Acute decompensated HF with cardiogenic shock (inotrope)' | 'Tachycardia, ventricular arrhythmias, hypotension'. '"Platelet inhibitors" / Cilostazol^a / Dipyridamole^b': 'In platelets: ↑ cAMP → inhibition of platelet aggregation' | 'Intermittent claudication / Stroke or TIA prevention (with aspirin) / Cardiac stress testing (dipyridamole only, due to coronary vasodilation) / Prevention of coronary stent restenosis' | 'Nausea, headache, facial flushing, hypotension, abdominal pain'. Footnotes: a 'Cilostazol is a PDE-3 inhibitor, but due to its indications is categorized as a platelet inhibitor together with dipyridamole.'; b 'Dipyridamole is a nonspecific PDE inhibitor, leading to inhibition of platelet aggregation. It also prevents adenosine reuptake by platelets → ↑ extracellular adenosine → ↑ vasodilation.' Carried VERBATIM as the note's two table blocks and conveyed as ONE original KYP isoform-fork map (the mechanism strip, the isoform fork cards, the nonspecific pair, the use grid, the caution strip, the boundary strip, the reading-rule footer) — no artwork reproduced.
